facts.text: Semantic or object-list replay supplies decision software with recorded or ground-truth object lists containing type, position and speed instead of raw sensor data, testing only warning and braking logic.
facts.quote: Semantic replay feeds the decision software not with raw sensor data but with a list of objects (type, position, speed), either recorded or taken from ground truth, so that only the warning and braking logic is tested.

facts.text: Semantic replay bypasses perception and supplies object lists directly in common coordinates together with machine state.
facts.quote: Semantic replay skips perception and supplies that list directly, in common coordinates together with machine state.

facts.text: Semantic replay exercises decision logic, warning stages and brake-request rules independently of sensor type.
facts.quote: The decision logic, warning stages and brake-request rules are then exercised independent of any sensor type.

facts.text: Semantic replay can run open loop using lists as recorded or closed loop using lists regenerated as the virtual machine slows.
facts.quote: It can run open loop (lists as recorded) or closed loop (lists regenerated as the virtual machine slows)

facts.text: Semantic replay is described as the cheapest way to sweep very large scenario sets because no rendering or ray tracing is involved.
facts.quote: It is the cheapest way to sweep very large scenario sets, because no rendering or ray tracing is involved

facts.text: The booklet's compute table rates logic and object-list braking tests as processor-dominant, with very high parallelism and suitability for commodity servers.
facts.quote: the booklet's compute table rates "logic and object-list braking tests" as processor-dominant with very high parallelism, suited to commodity servers

facts.text: Semantic replay proves thresholds, warning logic, threat assessment and brake-request logic.
facts.quote: It proves thresholds, warning logic, threat assessment and brake-request logic.

facts.text: Semantic replay cannot prove perception and can hide sensor latency, occlusion, false detections and range or classification errors because semantic replay assumes perception has already succeeded.
facts.quote: It cannot prove perception, and it can hide sensor latency, occlusion, false detections and range or classification errors, because it assumes perception has already succeeded

facts.text: ASAM OSI (Open Simulation Interface) provides standard interfaces between environment, sensor, fusion and function models, including ground-truth interfaces, for semantic replay tests.
facts.quote: ASAM OSI (Open Simulation Interface) provides standard interfaces between environment, sensor, fusion and function models, including ground-truth interfaces, for exactly this kind of test

facts.text: The first level of the booklet's multi-fidelity architecture consists of deterministic functional and object-list tests for millions of braking-logic combinations.
facts.quote: The first level of the booklet's multi-fidelity architecture is "deterministic functional and object-list tests for millions of braking-logic combinations"

facts.text: The booklet recommends starting software-in-the-loop (SIL) testing with semantic inputs before adding realistic sensor error models.
facts.quote: semantic inputs are where the booklet says software-in-the-loop (SIL) testing should start, before realistic sensor error models are added
